clue.text: Those folk, hard to miss, quietly spoken, and not around for long

indicators.note: the hard letter is to be missed out, so it is dropped from the word for those folk

parts.note: them refers to those people
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
oral means spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: A group of quiet, softly spoken people who will not be staying long.
explanation.definitionFit: Temporal can mean temporary or worldly, belonging to passing time rather than eternity, so lasting only briefly.

clue.text: We dart and tear around hopelessly — and fail to progress

indicators.note: moving around hopelessly means the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: People dashing about aimlessly and getting nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is only a link joining the two halves of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread water, literally staying afloat in one spot, is the idiom for making no headway.

clue.text: Stick raised for attack

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: gum is glue, used to stick

explanation.surface: A stick lifted high in order to strike someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To mug someone is to assault and rob them in the street.

clue.text: Food nothing at all? Not quite — this person tucked in

indicators.note: tucked in means the person is slipped inside the other letters

parts.note: O is the round figure zero, nothing

indicators.note: not quite means the last letter of the word all is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, then shortened
the speaker, this person, is me

explanation.surface: Was it no food at all? Not quite, as the writer happily tucked in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked in' looks like eating heartily, but it is the container signal; 'Not quite' trims the final letter of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Oatmeal is ground oats, a food made into porridge and baking.

clue.text: Making better sermon, perhaps, after declaration by priest?

indicators.note: by places the priest's name right beside the declaration
after puts the sermon after the declaration by the priest

parts.note: I am, a declaration of identity, shortened to am
Eli is the priest in the Old Testament book of Samuel, a crossword favourite
a sermon is an example of an oration, a formal speech

explanation.surface: A priest opens with a declaration and then preaches, hoping to make things better.
explanation.walkthrough: Read AM ELI as the priest's 'I am Eli', the declaration.
explanation.definitionFit: Amelioration is the act of improving something, so a noun for the process of improvement.

clue.text: Rants, seeing no one does business

indicators.note: seeing no one means the word for rants is seen without the letter for one

parts.note: tirades are long angry rants
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone who rants and finds nobody listening ends up doing deals.
explanation.definitionFit: To trade is to buy and sell, so trades means carries on commerce, the verb matching does business.

clue.text: Bringing up son — no good providing fruity nibbles?

indicators.note: no good says the letter for good is to be left out

parts.note: raising a child is bringing it up
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent bringing up a son who is no good, offered dried fruit snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Raisins are dried grapes, eaten as small sweet snacks, so fruit nibbles.

clue.text: Disorder with Eden garment being abandoned?

indicators.note: abandoned suggests loose and unrestrained, so the letters are let loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: Adam and Eve's fig leaves cast off in Eden, leading to a fall into chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Derangement means mental disturbance or confusion, a state of being out of order.

clue.text: Son on edge — one of those in rescue vessel?

definitions.text: one of those in rescue vessel?

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
a hem is the edge of cloth

explanation.surface: A son on the brink, wondering if he will be saved aboard a lifeboat.
explanation.walkthrough: Shem was one of Noah's sons, saved from the Flood in the ark.
explanation.definitionFit: Shem was a son of Noah, one of the eight people carried through the Flood on the ark.

clue.text: Cardinal showing gravity — not weak, even at the end

indicators.note: at the end places the poetic word for even after the rest
not weak tells us to remove the letter standing for weak from the word for gravity

parts.note: weight is heaviness, the effect of gravity
W is an abbreviation for weak, used in physics for the weak force
e'en is the poetic contraction of even

explanation.surface: A churchman of the Roman Church who displays solemn gravity and never weakens, even at the last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a churchman, but here it is a cardinal number. E'EN is the old poetic shortening of 'even'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal numbers are the counting numbers one, two, three and so on, and eighteen is one of them.

clue.text: President as leader of Republicans featured in article

indicators.note: featured in says the leader's letter appears within the word for article

parts.note: a piece is an article, as in a newspaper piece

indicators.note: leader of picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A president who leads the Republicans is the subject of a newspaper article.
explanation.walkthrough: Franklin Pierce was the 14th President of the United States, ironically a Democrat rather than a Republican.
explanation.definitionFit: Franklin Pierce served as the fourteenth head of state of the United States, from 1853 to 1857.

clue.text: What could be a drape where troops assemble

parts.note: the first word with its letters ground up, crushed into a new order, could spell a drape

explanation.surface: A curtain hung at the place where soldiers gather.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: PARADE, ground (mixed up), gives A DRAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A parade ground is the open square where soldiers fall in for drill and inspection.

clue.text: Broadcast from detectives beside house to the west of the country

indicators.note: beside means the next piece is placed alongside the detectives
in an across clue, west is left, so the house comes before the country

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors
a semi is a semi-detached house, very common in Britain
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A news bulletin from police detectives at a house in the west of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi is a semi-detached house, one of a pair joined by a shared wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissemination is the spreading of information widely, which is what broadcasting news does; noun matches noun.

clue.text: Homeless gent must be heard immediately

indicators.note: must be heard says the words are taken by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: a stray is homeless and a toff is a posh gent; stray toff sounds like the answer

explanation.surface: A down-and-out gentleman insists on being listened to right now.
explanation.walkthrough: A toff is British slang for an upper-class gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight off is an idiom for at once, without delay.

clue.text: Bad, mad true drunk is portrayed in outline

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and disordered, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A rogue, crazy and genuinely intoxicated, is sketched roughly.
explanation.definitionFit: To adumbrate is to sketch or foreshadow, giving only a faint indication of something.

clue.text: Trouble squashing publicity when bloomers become evident?

indicators.note: squashing means the trouble word presses around the publicity letters, holding them inside

parts.note: to ail is to trouble, as in what ails you
PR is public relations, publicity

explanation.surface: A problem crushes the publicity effort just when embarrassing gaffes come to light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomers' looks like blunders or underwear; here they are flowers, which bloom in spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring flowers come into blossom during this month, so it is a time when blooms first appear.

clue.text: Does tar at sea notice possible place for anchorage?

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A sailor, a tar, wonders whether a posted notice marks a spot where ships may anchor.
explanation.walkthrough: A tar is an old word for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadstead is a sheltered stretch of water near shore where ships can safely lie at anchor.

clue.text: Huge group of soldiers seizing part of hospital — big shock may be felt there

definitions.text: big shock may be felt there

indicators.note: seizing means the outer words grab and hold the hospital department inside

parts.note: epic means huge in scale
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A large military force takes over a hospital ward, causing great alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: The epicentre is the point on the surface directly above an earthquake's origin, where the tremor is strongest.

clue.text: Not all heard rumours — one's needed to listen!

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Gossip only partly caught, and the ear is needed to hear it all.
explanation.definitionFit: The eardrum is the membrane in the ear that vibrates with sound, essential for hearing.

clue.text: A smile from one side to another on journey?

definitions.text: from one side to another on journey?

parts.note: to beam is to smile broadly

explanation.surface: A traveller smiling from ear to ear across the whole trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeam describes a bearing at right angles to a ship's keel, directly out to the side of a vessel underway.

clue.text: Like a number commonly seen having a coffee

parts.note: everyday numerals are Arabic ones, so an ordinary number is Arabic

explanation.surface: A familiar number shows up while someone has a coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabica is the main species of coffee bean, grown widely and prized for flavour.

clue.text: Bedlam as terrorist is seen to do this — coastal officer appears

parts.words: Bedlam as terrorist is seen to do this
parts.note: the words bedlaM AS TERrorist hold the word MASTER inside them, so they can be said to harbour, or shelter, a master

explanation.surface: Chaos as a terrorist is spotted sheltering someone, and a port official turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do this' points at the answer's first word as a verb: the clue's run of letters harbours MASTER. Bedlam was London's notorious lunatic asylum.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbourmaster is the official in charge of a port, overseeing berthing and shipping on the coast.

clue.text: What one discusses is tailless antelope

indicators.note: tailless means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a topic is a subject under discussion

explanation.surface: A conversation about an antelope with no tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The topi is a large African antelope of the savannah, related to the hartebeest.

clue.text: One senses them being so backward, gloomy inside

indicators.note: inside places the gloomy word within the reversed letters
backward tells us to read the word so from right to left

parts.note: dour means gloomy and stern

explanation.surface: A sensitive person feels everything as backward and gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Smells are perceived by the sense of smell, so they are things a person senses through the nose.

clue.text: What accounts for insect being drunk maybe — or cow?

indicators.note: what accounts for, or explains, the insect's state is drink in it, so the pieces are set drink first, insect last

parts.note: rum is one thing that may be drunk, a drink
being in is being inside, so the word in is drawn from being here
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about why an insect might be tipsy, or a cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What accounts for' asks what would explain a tipsy insect: RUM IN ANT, the drink inside the insect, read straight through.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle chew the cud, bringing food back from the stomach to chew again, which makes them cud-chewers.

clue.text: Bow of rescue vessel in the sound

indicators.note: in the sound means spoken aloud, with a pun on a sound, a coastal channel

parts.note: Noah's ark saved his family and the animals

explanation.surface: The front of a lifeboat out in a coastal channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow' looks like the front of a boat, but here it is a curve.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc is a curved line, the shape of a bow or archer's bow.

clue.text: One learner thus gives family disrepute

indicators.note: thus gives family says that the two letters, set as the answer describes, turn into the word family

parts.note: one is I and learner is L, the letters on a British learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A single learner driver is enough to bring shame on the whole household.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as IN FAMY: I and L placed in FAMY spell FAMILY. L is the learner plate on British cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Infamy is notoriety and public disgrace, a bad reputation, matching disrepute as a noun.

clue.text: A theologian holding leading position, wanting the church improved?

indicators.note: holding means the theologian's letters wrap around what follows

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity
the van is the front of an army, the leading position
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A churchman scholar holds a top post but still wants the church to get better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' joins the church letters to the leading position, both held inside the theologian.
explanation.definitionFit: Advanced means moved forward or developed further, close to made better, hence the question mark.
